rules.rule: Budget only overlapping allocations before the next mandatory fresh free-space check; never waive later build, backup or stop capacity.
rules.initialization: No schema/config/production/Acceptance-data write. Fetch subprocess removes its own Git store on EXIT before prepare. Archive still includes current Git occupation in actual available; expired allocations are not added to later heavy work. Installed old tool refuses executable-policy refresh, explicit install required.
rules.dateAndPermission: Pinned Acceptance database identity, all storage path/metric validation and readonly peer collection retained at download/archive. Build/backup/stop rewrite, backup, WAL, logs, operating margin and fail-before-stop dispatch remain unchanged; no capacity bypass or cleanup.
rules.expectation: Sixteen actual Python boundary tests plus original shell dispatch with real estimator: download/archive succeeds then build, backup or stop insufficient reports refusal before any stop/apply/activate effect. Old production/runtime isolation, verified history recovery and original update semantics pass.

rules.rule: A nonempty installed matching Acceptance or production lock provides dependency sizing evidence with 50percent margin, never implicit permission to reuse dependencies.
rules.initialization: Both current dependency roots are measured. Exactly matching package-lock bytes and positive installed size are required, maximum matching size selected; floor512MiB. Missing/changed/no installed match keeps floor2GiB. Actual locked npm install, immutable tools, existing release and backup retention remain unchanged.
rules.dateAndPermission: Read existing local lock/size only; no site credentials, account/config change, install, cleanup or deployment performed. Original worker build checks and production locks remain authoritative.
rules.expectation: Old production lock plus matching Acceptance400MiB measures600MiB. Unknown and missing target lock retain2GiB; original updater and deployment contract tests pass. This is local estimation correctness, not a claim of exact现场 capacity or deployment success.
